meta.note: Excerpts from public USAJOBS announcements (works of the US government, public domain), lightly trimmed. Labels and tiers were assigned by hand to show how the cascade divides the work; they are not output from the production model.

segments.text: Perform data acquisition, processing, and cleaning of large data sets
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A task with no heading phrase a rule knows; the encoder labels it from its content.

segments.text: Leverage machine learning and other analytical techniques to interpret large amounts of data to gain insight and identify patterns
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: Another task; the encoder handles it like the one before.

segments.text: Deliver written status updates, formal technical reports, and briefings to leaders
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: Plain task wording: the encoder's everyday work.

segments.text: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service
segments.label: experience
segments.why: A fixed federal phrase (“specialized experience equivalent to”): a rule matches it.

segments.text: Experience using cybersecurity principles, secure software development / acquisition, data security, risk management processes
segments.label: skills
segments.why: Starts like experience but lists skills; the encoder reads past the first word.

segments.text: Degree; Mathematics, statistics, computer science, data science or field directly related to the position.
segments.label: education
segments.why: “Degree;” followed by fields of study: a rule matches it.

segments.text: Combination of education and experience: Courses equivalent to a major field of study (30 semester hours) as shown in paragraph A above, plus additional education or appropriate experience
segments.label: education
segments.why: Trades education against experience and points back to another paragraph; left for the LLM.

segments.text: Must be a U.S. Citizen
segments.label: conditions
segments.why: A citizenship phrase: a rule matches it.

segments.text: Employee must obtain/maintain a Non-Critical Sensitive (Secret) security clearance
segments.label: conditions
segments.why: A requirement with no fixed phrase; the encoder labels it.

postings.title: Registered Nurse, Geriatrics and Extended Care

segments.text: Will perform job duties independently and in accordance with established departmental and hospital procedures.
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A duty without a known phrase; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: Reports to the CLC Nurse Manager and Assistant Nurse Manager, but must work in collaboration with the Charge Nurses, Staff Nurses, Nursing Assistants, Medical Support Assistants, Social Workers, Minimum Data Set Coordinators, Restorative and Recreational care, and Providers of the assigned team.
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: Long, but plainly about the work; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: English Language Proficiency. In accordance with 38 U.S.C. 7403(f), no person shall serve in direct patient care positions unless they are proficient in basic written and spoken English.
segments.label: skills
segments.why: A statute about language: a skill or a condition of employment? It needs judgement, so the LLM decides.

segments.text: Graduate of a school of professional nursing approved by the appropriate accrediting agency and accredited by one of the following accrediting bodies: The Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).
segments.label: education
segments.why: Names accrediting bodies rather than a degree; the encoder still reads it as education.

segments.text: Current, full, active, and unrestricted registration as a graduate professional nurse in a State, Territory or Commonwealth (i.e., Puerto Rico) of the United States, or the District of Columbia.
segments.label: certifications
segments.why: “Unrestricted registration as a graduate professional nurse”: a licence phrase a rule matches.

segments.text: Installing, modifying, repairing, loading and testing systems, circuits, equipment and controls
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A task; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: Interpreting and applying the National Electrical Code, local codes, building plans, blueprints, wiring diagrams
segments.label: skills
segments.why: Listed as a duty but names knowledge; the encoder labels it a skill.

segments.text: Determining location of existing electrical devices and service entrances
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A task; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: Planning and laying out work, tracing hard-to-locate defects or problems
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A task; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: Installing, modifying, repairing, and maintaining electrical lines, circuits, systems
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A task; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: …install, configure, troubleshoot, and provide maintenance and training in response to customer requirements
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A task cut from a longer sentence; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: Provide Tier II support for end-user hardware failures
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A task; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: Re-image customer workstations and resolve complex problems
segments.label: responsibilities
segments.why: A task; the encoder labels it.

segments.text: Detect damaged or lost files, optimize disk management, measure system performance, control system security
segments.label: skills
segments.why: A run of abilities; the encoder labels them as skills.

segments.text: Must obtain and maintain Security+ Certification within six (6) months of appointment
segments.label: certifications
segments.why: A named certification (Security+): a rule matches it.

segments.text: Incumbent must complete appropriate training and obtain required certifications IAW DoDI 8140 or DOD 8570.01M.
segments.label: certifications
segments.why: Names a policy, not a certification, so no rule fires; the encoder still reads it as a certification requirement.
